correctness.rationale: All distinct short-arc diagonal pairs are disjoint, properly nested, or crossing. The first two have exact independent-triangulation squared Catalan inclusion probabilities, with ordered multiplicities n(n-r-s-1) and 2n(r-s+1); crossing pairs contribute zero. Independent exhaustive enumeration of all polygon triangulation pairs through nine vertices agrees with the resulting exact factorial moments, with 106 exact assertions in check.py. Uniform Catalan asymptotics and summable dominated convergence show the disjoint contribution tends to the squared first moment and the nested contribution tends to \(2K\) times the first moment, \(K=4/\pi-1\) by a beta integral. The same argument with weights proves the general covariance functional. No finite experiment is used as an infinite proof.

value.rationale: A diagonal with short-side index of order \(\sqrt n\) belongs to both random triangulations with probability of order \(n^{-3/2}\), while there are order \(n^{3/2}\) candidate diagonals in any fixed positive band. This is a natural rare-event window in geometric Catalan structures. Its coincidences are not second-order Poisson: nested families persist, yielding a universal, strictly greater than one Fano ratio \(8/\pi-1\), independent of band. The full compactly-supported test-function covariance makes the insight applicable to rescaled length statistics and distinguishes it from an arbitrary finite computation.
